content.title: About
content.content: Vodka and soda is a simple cocktail made of plain vodka diluted with carbonated water (soda). The drink has a light, refreshing taste, moderate strength, and is often served in tall glasses over ice.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The vodka‑soda combination originated in the United States in the early 1920s as a lighter alternative to straight vodka.
Vodka and soda is frequently used as a base for more complex cocktails such as the Vodka Tonic or Vodka Spritz.
Carbonated water helps soften the perception of alcohol on the palate, making the drink more “drinkable.”
In some countries it is served as a “shot‑cocktail,” where a shot of vodka is chased with soda.
Soda can be plain or flavored (lemon, lime, grapefruit), altering the flavor profile of the drink.

items.title: Moderate consumption
items.content: When consumed in moderation (1‑2 servings per week) vodka and soda can provide relaxation without a large calorie load.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Carbonated water contributes to overall fluid intake, especially when the drink is made without added sugar.

items.title: Low sugar content
items.content: Unlike many mixed drinks, vodka and soda contains virtually no sugar, making it a better choice for those monitoring blood glucose.

items.title: Alcohol intoxication
items.content: Vodka is a high‑proof spirit; even when diluted it can cause intoxication and associated risks.

items.title: Stomach irritation
items.content: Carbonated water may increase bloating or discomfort in people with sensitive stomachs.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Alcohol can amplify the effects of certain medications; limit intake when taking drugs.

content.title: How to Make
content.content: Pour 40‑50 ml of vodka into a tall glass over ice, add 150‑200 ml of cold soda water, stir gently. Optionally garnish with a lemon or lime wedge.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store vodka in a tightly sealed bottle in a cool, dark place. Use fresh soda water, and keep opened soda bottles refrigerated and consumed within 2‑3 days.
